headline: High: shared filesystem writes and shared-context skills create default conflict and leakage pathways; prompt-injection risk is lower because A is non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is content-writing and non-runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B's outputs by default. Agent B writes files and its skills reference each other and build on shared context, which creates a manual or file-based bridge if A's content is copied into B. The pathway exists but is not default and the blast radius is limited to content manipulation.
conditions: IF A's generated text is copied into B's shared skill files or prompts, B may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions.
IF B parses file contents from .agents/skills or .claude/skills as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Review copied prompt text before placing it into B's skill files.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared-context files for B.
Use a manual approval step before B executes instructions from files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied prompt content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B reads and writes filesystem content and can call external APIs. If A's outputs are stored in B's workspace, B can transmit that content to GitHub or marketing-skills.com. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default file-based workflows, though A itself is not a data source.
conditions: IF A's outputs are saved into B's workspace files, B can read them.
IF B sends workspace-derived content to GitHub or marketing-skills.com, copied A content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive A outputs in B's workspace.
Restrict B's API calls to non-sensitive repositories.
Separate local folders for A and B.
Review outbound requests from B before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce content-classification filters on B's API uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write surface, but B has filesystem write, subprocess, and allowlisted network egress, plus support for multiple instances. If both agents operate on the same directory, B can overwrite or race on files that A's content pipeline depends on. Because B's concurrency is explicit and A lacks isolation controls, the shared-write conflict is dangerous by default once co-located.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same workspace directory, B can overwrite files used by A's content workflow.
IF multiple B instances run concurrently on shared files, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Add file locks around shared outputs.
Back up workspace files before B writes.
requires-engineering: implement transactional writes for B.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces prompt/content material and B's skills build on shared context, so B may treat A's output as authoritative input. B also has API and filesystem actions, which means a mistaken A artifact can cascade into published marketing content or repository changes. The chain is plausible, but B can still be manually reviewed, so this is not high.
conditions: IF A's output is imported into B's shared context, B may reuse it without verification.
IF B publishes or commits content derived from A, errors can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require human review of A output before B uses it.
Mark A-derived text as untrusted in B's context.
Compare B drafts against source material before publishing.
Limit B to draft-only mode for A-derived content.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B only shows generic marketing content handling and external API calls. The evidence does not prove a compliance breach, but B's outbound API use means any regulated data placed into its workspace could leave the local environment. A is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's workspace, B may transmit it to external services.
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees, B's documented surfaces do not show them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's workspace.
Use B only for non-sensitive marketing content.
Review outbound API destinations before use.
Set a short local retention policy for B files.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
